## Purpose

If you can read this as a **PDF**, Quarto, R and Typst are all working on your computer. You are ready for Wednesday's workshop.

This document uses `airquality`, a small dataset that comes with R: daily air-quality measurements in New York, May to September 1973.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
```

## Summary statistics

```{r}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Average ozone and temperature by month, New York, 1973."
airquality |>
  group_by(Month) |>
  summarise(
    `Days measured` = n(),
    `Mean ozone (ppb)` = round(mean(Ozone, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    `Mean temperature (F)` = round(mean(Temp), 1)
  ) |>
  mutate(Month = month.name[Month]) |>
  kable()
```

## A figure

```{r}
#| label: fig-scatter
#| fig-cap: "Hotter days had higher ozone concentrations."
#| warning: false
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3.6
ggplot(airquality, aes(x = Temp, y = Ozone)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, colour = "darkorange", se = TRUE) +
  labs(x = "Daily maximum temperature (F)", y = "Ozone (parts per billion)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## A statistic in the text

The correlation between temperature and ozone is
`r round(cor(airquality$Temp, airquality$Ozone, use = "complete.obs"), 2)`.
That number was calculated by R when this document was rendered, not typed by hand.

See you Wednesday!
